newsitem.title: UK: Russian oil industry unhappy with govt reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Russian oil industry unhappy with govt reshuffle.

text.p: Senior members of Russia's oil industry and Duma lower house of parliament told a conference on Thursday they were unhappy with President Yeltsin's government reshuffle earlier this week.
In particular they criticised the decision to place several ministries under the control of an enlarged ministry of the economy led by Anatoly Chubais.
"A lot has been said about the personal changes. But what is revolutionary is the principle on which the government is patterned," said Mikhail Zadornov, chairman of the Duma's budget committee.

"It's a kind of modular system, there are no longer different ministries with different areas. All will be under the ministry of the economy. All other ministries will be departments under this," he added.
Viktor Ott, first deputy minister of fuel and energy, voiced his reservations in a news conference.

"It's not just because I work in it that I think Russia needs a body like the Ministry of Fuel and Energy," he said. "Our ministry is already undergoing restructuring. We are already setting up conditions and priorities for producers."

Artur Chilingarov, deputy chairman of the Duma, was also concerned. "I always thought certain basic ministries should be preserved. Russia is not yet ready for the functional way of running the country that is being proposed.
"Certain fundamental ministries are needed. That's why I'm not very optimistic about the proposed reorganisation of the government," he said.
